review_description: I went with DES mainly because I decided on micro inverters over string inverters.  Right from the start DES were very punctual and efficient.  (Another local company failed to turn up on two occasions to give a quote....!)  The DES salesperson was always punctual, very knowledgable and was happy to answer my many questions.  The installer did a great job; it took three and a half days.  Getting the cabling from roof to meter box was a bit challenging but he came up with a great solution - very neat and tidy.  He also didn't mind me seeing what they were doing from time to time and was also happy to answer my questions.  Within hours of the installer 'signing off' the job I was producing power.  The Enphase APP is also quite informative.The system was the dearest of the quotes I received but hopefully it will prove to be of high quality in the long run.From my experience I recommend DES.

I went with DES Electrical as I could get more watts on my limited roof space with the sunpower maxeon 5 panels at 410 watt each all with emphases microenvrters.DES have been excellent to deal with so now i am a electricity producer should have done it years ago and thank you Finn for your site and knowledge on what’s what

If you do not use the power when it is produced you lose it to the grid for a small amount of compensation.   I use a hybrid system using solar tubes for hot water and solar panels for electricity. The solar tubes are excellent generating hot water for most of the year, storage is obviously included.  However I would assume that if you used your solar panels to heat the water and had the hot water cylinder on a time switch, your wastage back to the grid would be negligible.  The solar tubes produce the equivalent of 1.5kwh.  The feed in meter gives you the total of unused power fed into the grid from the panels, and the charged power taken from the grid.  Which is basically everything you need to know.  Power production on a dull day is negligible, hot water production is less affected.

While possibly not the cheapest, I found their costing very competitive and the quality of job was worth the few extra dollars that it may have cost.

We chose an Enphase micro system, as it is more or less future prove - to a certain extent. The supplier explained everything very thoroughly. This system makes it easy to add storage once it becomes available in 2016. We'll need storage in order to make the investment pay and to get full benefits from the installation. It will bring the cost of the full installation to about $15.000 or close, but it should mean that we will almost wipe our electricity bill apart from the 3 winter months. Currently we import too much back into the grid, which is uneconomical with an import tariff of only 6cents.
